newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy court says ex-minister overspent on Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy court says ex-minister overspent on Albania.

text.p: Italy's Court of Accounts on Monday accused a former foreign minister of misuse of public money by choosing a supplier that cost more than others for an aid mission to Albania in the early 1990s.

The court, which monitors public spending, said it believed ex-foreign minister Gianni De Michelis awarded a contract to a company to supply food and medicine to Albania although it charged 90 million lire ($56,000) more than others.

De Michelis, a former Socialist who lost his place in parliament after a corruption scandal swept Italy in 1992, will be required to testify before the court on the alleged overspending. The court did not set a date for the hearing.
It said the company, which has since gone out of business, was chosen without appropriate selection procedures being followed and said De Michelis had ultimate responsibility.
The Italian government was a leading provider of aid to Albania in the early 1990s when mass unrest after the fall of communism brought tens of thousands of refugees to Italy's southern shores.
Italy is now leading international efforts to help the impoverished Balkan nation again after it fell into chaos this year following the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes.

The flamboyant de Michelis, known for his love of disco dancing, has already been sentenced to four years in prison in a separate case for taking kickbacks in exchange for supporting motorway construction in the northeast Veneto region.
